long_biography.plain_text:
Robert A. Iger reshaped Disney through a strategy centred on creative brands, international growth and new distribution. After rising from studio-supervision work at ABC to lead its television operations, he joined Disney's senior management through the companies' merger and became chief executive in 2005.

He rebuilt relations with Pixar before acquiring the animation studio, then extended the same brand-led strategy to other entertainment businesses. Shanghai Disney Resort expanded the company's physical presence, while Disney+ moved its content directly to subscribers. Iger later left the company and returned for a second chief-executive term. Josh D'Amaro succeeded him in March 2026, closing Iger's second period at the helm.
